method: Headless Chromium 1248 (Playwright 1.63), shipped posthogInitScript() loader, real posthog-js served from t.hagicode.com/static/array.js (SDK 1.444.0 static assets). Event and recording POSTs to t.hagicode.com stubbed and recorded; no request left the machine. Harness overrides: a non-HeadlessChrome user agent and navigator.webdriver = false, because posthog-js drops every event from a bot-looking browser before any request is made.

cases.description: Loader only, no replay calls. Recording is on by project default.
set_config({ disable_session_recording: true }) and stopSessionRecording() queued right after the loader, in the same synchronous frame.
As 1.1, with the remote config answer delayed by 1500 ms, to check that a late config does not re-enable recording.
As 1.1, then set_config({ disable_session_recording: false }) and startSessionRecording() after the visitor opts in, on the same page.

conclusion: The queued calls keep /s/ silent while events flow and survive a late remote config. An explicit opt-in starts recording on the same page. The init-time flag fallback (design decision 6) is not needed. Activity matters: the recorder flushes only after DOM or pointer changes, so each case drives mouse moves and DOM mutations before it counts /s/ requests.
caveat: One run per case. Re-run the probe before changing the posthog-js version or the loader.
